Colorizing a field in the final colorization pass is far cheaper than during ray-marching, because the color is evaluated once per pixel after the march completes rather than at every march step.

op:Lib.numbers.int.basic.RandomChoiceInd.note: Turn an incoming index into a fresh random index that never repeats the same value twice in a row — ideal for shuffling through images without two identical frames back to back.

op:Lib.numbers.float.basic.Modulo.note: Wrap a rising counter back to a beat-relative phase, e.g. to retrigger a [Bloom] flash once per bar.

get longer trails from fewer points by inserting a filter between two particle systems: divide MaxParticleCount for the step count, advance the start index with a frame counter, and use the built-in modulo input to wrap; splitting an existing connection line by clicking it inserts the math op inline.

ui:SymbolBrowser.note: Live thumbnails now render for every operator and its siblings in the browser, so you can eyeball what an op produces before placing it.

click once on an operator's output (or in the empty space below it) to get context-aware suggestions ranked by how frequently that connection occurs; placing downstream ops below rather than beside keeps the graph auto-grouped, which suits post-processing stacks.

Long-press the canvas to open the operator browser and search by synonym — typing "LFO" finds the oscillator value op even though that's not its name; report missing synonyms so the description can be extended.

Select several operators, drag out one connection group, and the browser lists every op with a matching multi-input so you can fan many sources into one; press G afterward to auto-layout the new group.

op:Lib.numbers.bool.logic.Trigger.note: Trigger-play a clip from an external event by feeding a stopwatch's elapsed seconds into the video's time input and starting/stopping the watch with the trigger, with looping off so the clip halts at its end.

op:Lib.mesh.generate.TorusMesh.note: Searching "donut" yields it (a torus is the graphics term); hover its output to confirm it's a mesh buffer, then click the output to get usage-ranked suggestions for what to wire next.
Thin the ring by dialing its thickness/inner-radius down (here to ~0.03–0.15) so it reads as a slender band rather than a fat donut.

op:Lib.render.postfx.ProjectLight.note: current shadow options: a projector-style light with halfway-decent single-source shadows, directional draw-with-shadow, and a point-light variant using percentage-closer filtering for slightly blurred edges; ambient occlusion softens shading but is no substitute for real shadows.

op:Lib.mesh.draw.DrawMeshWithShadow.note: current shadow options: a projector-style light with halfway-decent single-source shadows, directional draw-with-shadow, and a point-light variant using percentage-closer filtering for slightly blurred edges; ambient occlusion softens shading but is no substitute for real shadows.

op:Lib.image.fx.blur.Bloom.note: Glows only from areas brighter than 1.0, so pair it with HDR colours (e.g. an HDR step in a material's gradient) to make just the bright bands of a surface bleed light.

Its internal gradient colours the successive blur levels by distance from the source — and accepts transparent steps — so you can tint the outer glow a different hue or cut the core entirely for an underwater halo.
An expensive effect because it runs multiple blur cascades; at 8K those passes are what drops you off 60 fps, so it's a prime candidate to apply at a reduced resolution.

op:Lib.render.camera.Camera.note: Inject a second camera, rename it, and switch the output from auto to that named camera so you can fly an "edit camera" around a pinned background scene without disturbing the final composite camera.
Without a camera operator the viewer's own orbit isn't stored anywhere; add one and pin its output so dragging the view writes into saveable position parameters instead of a throwaway preview.

op:Lib.mesh.modify.TransformMesh.note: Choose it to move the geometry itself versus a downstream [Transform] that moves where the mesh is drawn; the distinction matters when later ops depend on point/object positions.

op:Lib.image.generate.basic.Blob.note: A soft procedural shape used as a fake drop-shadow texture under an object; its preview thumbnail inherits the output aspect ratio, which is why you give it a fixed resolution so it stays round.

Stack two image operators and they auto-snap into a chain that composites foreground over background at the target resolution; feathering the edge and dragging brightness down removes the colour fringe between fore- and background.

Even an 8x8 texture draws smoothly because sampling defaults to linear filtering (and can visibly wrap at edges); a per-drawer filter option exists only in some operators, prompting the feature request discussed next.
Add a negative-brightness blob over the image to make a vignette — darkening the corners with one shape, no dedicated effect needed.

op:Lib.mesh.generate.CylinderMesh.note: Build a small cylinder, reduce its segment detail and shrink its radius/height, then draw it stacked on a cube to compose a Lego-style brick from primitives.

op:Lib.mesh.generate.SphereMesh.note: Pair a primitive mesh with a draw operator to make geometry visible in the output; shrink the mesh radius before composing it with other shapes.

op:Lib.field.generate.vec3.ToroidalVorte.note: Twists particles into a torus/mushroom-cloud shape — faking such a swirl by hand turned out harder than driving it with this purpose-built field.

op:Lib.particle.force.VelocityForce.note: In a stack of guiding forces, a velocity push triggered on each note nudges particles forward for a beat-responsive surge.
Offers min and max speed clamps that map directly onto drone speed limits, but provides no acceleration limit, which would still need separate handling.

op:Lib.point.generate.SpherePoints.note: Replicate a small sphere of points on each emitter point, gradient-color them, and jitter their radial distance to build a soft scattered burst.
Raise the point count and shrink the radius to wrap a dense shell of points around an object; follow with a randomizer to break the too-perfect spherical surface.

op:Lib.point.sim.PointSimulation.note: Stamp/bake the carefully animated motion of a small control-point set so a downstream reconstructive force can guide the main ribbons precisely through the scene.

The legacy point-damper: it mutates the incoming buffer in place instead of copying it, so it smoothly interpolates positions toward a switched target and is ideal for de-noising jittery sampled or fed-back point data.

op:Lib.point.generate.PointsOnMesh.note: Scatter shaded point sprites (not spheres) across a loaded mesh's surface; the close-up fade-out seen here was flagged as a bug to fix.

op:Lib.point.modify.AttributesFromImageC.note: The current replacement for the obsolete [SamplePointAttributes_v1]: it reads an image's color channels onto point attributes the same way, just the newer operator.

op:Lib.render.transform.Group.note: Control+Shift+D duplicates with connections, correctly handling multi-inputs, and shaking an operator out now reconnects all compatible inputs rather than just the first.
Combining several meshes under one group yields a single combined mesh you can instance as a unit; reuse the same point set twice (one per sub-mesh) to scatter the composite.
Both expose an "is enabled" toggle, giving a second way to switch a scene branch on or off independent of any switch index.

op:Lib.flow.Execute.note: Use it over a Group when you only need to update/draw side-effects (set variables, run OSC output) with no data output — slightly faster since it skips the Group's transform/color overhead.
Both expose an "is enabled" toggle, giving a second way to switch a scene branch on or off independent of any switch index.

op:Lib.numbers.anim.time.StopWatch.note: Trigger-play a clip from an external event by feeding a stopwatch's elapsed seconds into the video's time input and starting/stopping the watch with the trigger, with looping off so the clip halts at its end.

op:Lib.numbers.anim.animators.AnimBoolea.note: A tidier on-beat trigger than wiring AnimValue by hand; drive it from the kick and feed its pulse into downstream animation. Internally identical to AnimValue but readable in the graph.
Set max-particle-count to -1 to size the buffer to the emit set, then emit only on a beat boolean to spawn a fixed batch and keep it alive indefinitely.

op:Lib.point.transform.OrientPoints.note: Orient scattered points to look toward a center, then scale to flatten them into oval/disc shards facing inward.

op:Lib.point.draw.DrawRayLines.note: Reach for it over [DrawLines] when a line can cross the camera plane (front to back): screen-space line drawing fails at that edge, so this skips corner mitering and stays seamless.
Prefer this over [DrawLines] for lines that run to infinity or past the camera: regular lines use screen space to size themselves and look wrong at extreme depths, whereas ray-lines stay consistent.

op:Lib.numbers.anim.animators.AnimInt.note: Same internals as AnimBoolean's counter but without the on-beat UI; the request raised here is to give it a modulo wrap and a speed factor so it counts within a range and loops.
A stepped integer animation with a deliberately odd weight/offset used to ride a polyrhythmic groove and gate when a counter advances.

op:Lib.numbers.bool.process.DelayBoolean.note: Distinct from DelayTriggerChange: it delays a boolean by a number of frames rather than holding a trigger open, useful for staggering events.

op:Lib.numbers.color.KeepColors.note: Continuously appends the incoming color into a fixed-length list each frame; drive its input from an [HSLToColor] over time to record a moving hue into a list you can then turn into a gradient or sample randomly.

op:Lib.numbers.floats.process.AnalyzeFlo.note: Feeds the quiz curve plotter: it derives the min/max range of a float list, padded a little, so the same range scales both the raster and the drawn curve consistently.

op:Lib.particle.force.SwitchParticleForc.note: Switch between alternate forces over an animation; note its -1 "disable all" magic index is why it's a switch, not a pick — flagged to be renamed to a pick-style operator.

op:Lib.point.draw.DrawRibbons.note: It needs correctly oriented points: if ribbons come out twisted, rotate the source points' orientation (about 90°) so the flat side faces the camera.

op:Lib.numbers.anim.animators.AnimValue.note: Zero out unwanted axes of the amplitude so an oscillation moves cleanly along one direction, and set the shape to sine for a slow, gradual back-and-forth.

op:Lib.point.modify.AddNoise.note: Most point modifiers expose a strength plus an F1/F2 picker that defaults to 1 (a neutral factor); pick F1 to gate the displacement per-point by a mask written upstream, or drive the noise amount from it.

ui:UserProject.note: The alpha build now creates its own versioned settings and project folder so a preview version can't silently corrupt the projects of your stable install.

keep repositories lean by git-ignoring the meta (thumbnails/variations), temp, and render folders, and expect a future breaking change that gathers all symbol files under a single Symbols folder for a cleaner project layout.

ui:Settings.note: A beat-sync offset adds a fixed lead time so playback runs earlier, compensating for LED controllers or devices with large output latency (e.g. half a second).
after plugging in a controller, rescan devices in settings; the first physical slider movement teaches the mapping to the connected parameter, then adjust the output range to fit.

op:Lib.numbers.int.basic.IntToFloat.note: the Step input is a float, so an integer division result must pass through an int-to-float conversion before it will connect; step then takes every Nth source point.

op:Lib.field.generate.sdf.CustomSDF.note: To detect externally when an SDF finished compiling, grab the raymarcher's second output (the generated shader-code string) and write it to a file as a completion signal — though file writing currently fails outside permitted paths under the new asset pipeline, logged as a to-do.

op:Lib.render.shading.SetFog.note: Fades the scene toward a colour by camera distance; with too few floor subdivisions the fade reveals banding across large triangles, so subdivide heavy geometry to keep distance-based shading smooth.

op:Lib.image.use.NormalMap.note: Set its output to RGB-signed to produce the negative-valued normal map that a screen-space force needs from an ordinary image.

op:Lib.field.space.TransformField.note: A new checkbox rotates the field's stored vectors along with the space when you rotate a vector field, otherwise direction and space disagree.

op:Lib.image.generate.noise.Grain.note: Set a non-zero speed (≈55) so the grain animates instead of sitting static, then keep the amount low so it's barely perceptible.
A built-in animation-speed knob avoids wiring a time source, but a "frozen" time mode is what lets a static result stop invalidating and actually cache instead of recomputing every frame.

op:Lib.image.fx.stylize.DetectEdges.note: Feed it a blurred noise pushed through [Steps] to get hard edges first; sample-radius, strength and contrast each shape the result, and a bias/gain knob would make a useful addition.

op:Lib.image.use.DepthBufferAsGrayScale.note: Exposes the z-buffer as an image you can feed into a mask blend to do per-depth post selection, the workaround for the missing per-object ID pass.

op:Lib.render.scene.DrawScene.note: Renders a loaded glTF scene and exposes overrides for the file's roughness and metallic values to tweak surface appearance.

op:Lib.io.file.WriteToFile.note: To detect externally when an SDF finished compiling, grab the raymarcher's second output (the generated shader-code string) and write it to a file as a completion signal — though file writing currently fails outside permitted paths under the new asset pipeline, logged as a to-do.

ui:ShaderNode.note: The generated effect ships as a detect-edges template with configurable settings (e.g. texture mode set to Wrap); its context menu adds typed input parameters such as a Vector2 split into floats wired to the shader's parameter buffer.

op:Lib.point.draw.DrawConnectionLines.note: Vertically-stacked operators fall back to a spline connection that can't be hovered or disconnected; this top-down wiring case is unfinished, which is why some wires won't detach.

op:Lib.mesh.modify.MeshFacesPoints.note: Re-implemented onto the new colored-point format with FX scale/stretch; a new option scales each point sprite by its polygon face area (computed trivially from the face's three vertices), great for spikes or cylinders that grow with face size.

op:Lib.mesh.modify.TransformMeshUVs.note: Its pivot is now centered so scaling grows from the middle; this is a breaking change from the old corner pivot, so older projects may shift.

op:Lib.mesh.generate.ExtrudeCurves.note: When you add an input parameter (here a scale factor that varies line thickness) you must triple-check it's actually wired to its [IntToFloat]/conversion node — an easy-to-miss disconnect after a version update.

op:Lib.image.transform.ImageFFT.note: Use this rather than the small built-in spectrum when you need a higher-resolution FFT: allocate a bigger buffer and you can analyze finer frequency detail.

op:Lib.point.generate.LinePoints.note: Combining two line sources — one with start/end colors, one slid through a color gradient — then layering a noise offset whose amount you crank via the infinity slider, since leaving point counts unmatched lets the offset bite.

ui:CurveEditor.note: Hundreds of keyframes squashed to a parameter's value range become practically invisible; auto-scaling the curve to the visible keyframes makes a dense track readable again.
Expand a parameter row to get an embedded curve editor aligned to the dope-sheet, so you can edit values and tangents in place instead of switching to a separate view.
A new "space evenly" command redistributes selected keyframes, but it aligns to the *strength* differences between keys rather than to uniform time — useful for cleaning up hand-tapped beats.

op:Lib.point.modify.SetPointAttributes.note: Spreads a gradient's colors across all points in a buffer so a color ramp maps onto a line set as a per-point attribute.
Smooth interpolation plus an asymmetric range gives a directional ramp — a sharp edge on one side, soft on the other — instead of a symmetric band.

op:Lib.field.generate.texture.Raster3dFi.note: A procedural 3D texture of grid lines/crosses you can transform, repeat-mirror, and combine with other fields — like the 2D raster pattern but defined throughout space; its line width and feather are adjustable.

op:Lib.numbers.int.logic.CountInt.note: increments by itself every rendered frame with nothing plugged in, and tries to detect the update cycle so loops or multiple graph evaluations per frame don't double-count.

get longer trails from fewer points by inserting a filter between two particle systems: divide MaxParticleCount for the step count, advance the start index with a frame counter, and use the built-in modulo input to wrap; splitting an existing connection line by clicking it inserts the math op inline.

op:Lib.numbers.int.process.FloatToInt.note: Flooring keeps the integer part (1.999 → 1), giving a step index you can use to pick list items per beat.
Convert a smoothly animated value into discrete steps by flooring it (or float-to-int and back), so a linear ramp becomes a staircase that advances exactly once per integer.

ui:Asset.note: Mip-maps store pre-scaled copies so a minified sprite samples a blurred level instead of aliasing; off by default for the small cost, only worth it when a textured thing changes size on screen (particles being the classic case).
Markdown is used throughout the help text, where square-bracket links open assets or operators directly in the library when clicked.

op:Lib.io.video.VideoDeviceInput.note: This is the webcam/capture-card operator (anything Windows exposes as a DirectX video device); its device list is the awkward part, currently pulled in via OpenCV.

It already exposes a flip-vertical flag, so flipping the camera image needs no separate [TransformImage] node — drop the extra op even at low resolution, on the principle that free optimizations are always worth taking.

op:Lib.render.scene.LoadGltfScene.note: Loads complete glTF scenes (not just single meshes), auto-combining textures into the correct channel maps for physically-based rendering; expand the scene setup to inspect each node and its material textures.

op:Lib.image.fx.distort.PolarCoordinates.note: Unwrap a radial image into its linear "straightened" form (or wrap the other way); changing the radius shows how the circular content maps to a flat strip.

op:Lib.flow.Switch.note: A switch's index selects which child branch is evaluated; -1 disables all, and unselected branches consume texture memory but no render cost, making it a cheap scene selector.

op:Lib.io.file.FilesInFolder.note: Procedurally driving a texture path (e.g. picking a string from its list) disposes and reloads the texture every change, spiking GPU memory; enable "cache resources" so repeatedly visited textures stay resident — the right call for VJ-style scrubbing, overkill otherwise.

op:Lib.numbers.anim.vj.ForwardBeatTaps.note: Forwards externally-tapped beats (e.g. an OSC tap from an iPad, or an Ableton click track sending one pulse per beat) into the beat system so someone else can tap for you.

op:Lib.field.use.SdfToVector.note: Returns a position in space near an SDF surface (computed from the field normal) so you can turn a distance field into a directional/vector field for forces.

op:Lib.particle.force.SnapToAnglesForce.note: Nudges particle velocities toward a set of defined angles, producing clean grid-like structures.

op:Lib.image.fx.stylize.ScreenCloseUp.note: A five-minute introduction to color grading in Tooll, centered on the lift/gamma/gain controls of the ColorGrade operator, reading the WaveForm operator's scope, and comparing before/after with CompareImages.

op:Lib.image.fx.stylize.Dither.note: Adds a retro dithered look; exposes blend modes plus bias-and-gain, exemplifying few-controls/wide-range effect design.

op:Lib.image.analyze.CompareImages.note: Load a reference photo and put it side-by-side (or wipe) against your render to rebuild a look methodically — the core technique for learning by reproducing an image.

op:Lib.image.analyze.ImageLevels.note: Drop it into a chain to read the average brightness/histogram of the current image, useful for judging how close to HDR your output is.
An "energy levels" analysis overlay that slices the image at a movable line and plots the colour there; a blinking warning marks where brightness clips and that highlight detail is lost for good.
Reads out the actual intensity along a slice as a graph overlay, a quick way to verify whether a gradient really reaches 0 and 1 or is clipped short.

Inspect an image's brightness histogram to tell whether transparent regions sit on black or white; that hidden base color decides how bloom/glow spreads and why two visually identical logos bloom differently.

ui:AssetLibrary.note: The asset library shows per-image thumbnails plus where each image is already used, and lets you swap one asset for another in place.

op:Lib.mesh.generate.LoadObj.note: Restricting a path parameter's file filter (here to .obj) makes the resource picker show only matching files; many operators were missing these filters and returned noise or nothing.

op:Lib.field.analyze.VisualizeFieldDista.note: Drop it in to actually see a field's distance bands while tuning a selection range, instead of guessing where the gradient sits.

ui:OperatorSettings.note: Finishing a new op cleanly: mark both inputs required, leave the strength unclamped so negative values still give useful results, and write a one-line description before merging.
Rename any operator by clicking its title field or selecting and pressing Return; a renamed op shows quote marks, and its underlying type is still readable in the top-left corner when selected.
Per-layout you can hide individual editor tabs and the hidden state is stored implicitly with each saved layout (F1/F2), giving a clean stage layout you toggle into.

op:Lib.numbers.floats.basic.ColorsToList.note: Builds a reusable color palette as a list you can feed into BuildGradient and rearrange, rather than hand-wiring individual colors.

ui:SearchWindow.note: Long-press the background and type to search; synonyms and fuzzy/substring matching mean "donut" finds the [TorusMesh] and even partial initials like "tm" rank [TorusMesh] and [TransformMesh] first — so small typos still land the op.

Pressing Ctrl-F on an empty search shows your recently visited operators as a history, not search results; arrow-down walks it, and Alt-Left/Right steps through your selection history like a code editor.
Typing `?` in the operator search returns a random operator, and cycling seeds yields fresh suggestions — a way to discover unfamiliar ops or set yourself a build challenge.

op:Lib.numbers.int.basic.IntDiv.note: get longer trails from fewer points by inserting a filter between two particle systems: divide MaxParticleCount for the step count, advance the start index with a frame counter, and use the built-in modulo input to wrap; splitting an existing connection line by clicking it inserts the math op inline.

op:Lib.image.color.Tint.note: Invert a grayscale image fastest by swapping the dark and light target colors; the same two color anchors plus contrast controls also give quick teal-orange style grades, slightly cheaper than a full color remap.

op:Lib.numbers.float.process.Damp.note: Feed an audio level through it to get instant attack and slow release (jump up immediately, ease down) — the practical way to get separate rise/fall smoothing from a single reaction value.

op:Lib.numbers.vec3.Vector3Gizmo.note: Plug it into a camera's target or position input to get a draggable in-viewport handle for that vector, instead of typing coordinates.

Ctrl-click a position parameter to extract it as a shared input you can feed to both a light and your shader offset, add a gizmo for on-screen handles, and note that all scene lights are already available in the shader as a Lights[] structure array you can index directly.

op:Lib.numbers.anim.time.HasTimeChanged.note: Its rewind-detect output wired to a reset clears a simulation every time you scrub time back, so tweaking an effect always restarts from a clean state.

op:Lib.image.use.UseTextureReference.note: Stash a render target under a named reference so a distant part of the graph can pull the same texture without a long wire across the canvas.

op:Lib.render.transform.SpreadLayout.note: Spreads connected inputs evenly in space, auto-spacing more steps as you add more connections — handy for laying out parallel test setups side by side.

op:Lib.render.gizmo.PlotValueCurve.note: Drop it on top of a group to graph a scalar over time inside the rendered scene — invaluable for debugging exported executables where you can't just open an extra output window.

op:Lib.numbers.float.adjust.Floor.note: Convert a smoothly animated value into discrete steps by flooring it (or float-to-int and back), so a linear ramp becomes a staircase that advances exactly once per integer.
